content.title: April's Pink Moon to pass over after Artemis II launch. When to watch
content.text: April 1, 2026, 3:22 p.m. CTApril's Pink Moon will coincide with the Artemis II launch on April 1.The Pink Moon will be visible in the Florida Panhandle after sunset, peaking around 9:12 p.m. CT.April's full moon received its Pink Moon nickname from a pink flower known as creeping phlox or moss phlox, not because of its color.With the launch of the Artemis II, which is set to put four astronauts on a flight around the moon for the first time since 1972, April 1 is suddenly a lot more exciting than the April Fools' Day jokes you've probably found yourself tripping over all day.A new mission to the moon isn't the only thing happening, though. April's Pink Moon will take the sky shortly after the Artemis astronauts launches at approximately 5:24 CT. Space fans really couldn't ask for a more perfect pairing.Floridians in the Panhandle will be able to catch the pink moon after the sun sets around 7:07 p.m. on April 1, according to the Farmer's Almanac. The full moon is expected to peak at 9:12 p.m.Here's what to know about April's Pink Moon.When is sunset on April 1 in the Florida Panhandle?The sun will start to set at around 7:07 p.m. CT on April 1, according to the Farmer's Almanac.When is the best time to see the pink moon in the Florida Panhandle?The best time to see the pink moon will be when it peaks at 9:12 p.m. CT.Why is it called the 'Pink Moon'?April's full moon is called the "Pink Moon" not because of its color, which will in reality have more of a golden hue, but because of the pink flower, known as creeping phlox or moss phlox, that was in full bloom during the month's full moon, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac.Other names for the moon include the following:The Sucker MoonBreaking Ice MoonBudding Moon of Plants and ShrubsMoon When the Ducks Come BackMoon When the Geese Lay EggsFrog MoonList of full moons in 2026The moon will be full on the following dates, according to the Farmer's Almanac:Pink Moon: Peaks April 1, at 10:12 p.m. ETFlower Moon: Peaks May 1, at 1:23 p.m. ETBlue Moon: Peaks May 31, at 4:45 a.m. ET. The blue moon occurs when two full moons occur in the same month. The last blue moon occurred on Aug. 19, 2024, according to Space.com.Strawberry Moon: Peaks June 29, at 7:57 p.m. ETBuck Moon: Peaks July 29, at 10:36 a.m. ETSturgeon Moon (partial lunar eclipse): Peaks Aug. 28, at 12:18 a.m. ETHarvest Moon: Peaks Sept. 26, at 12:49 p.m. ETHunter's Moon: Peaks Oct. 26, at 12:12 a.m. ETBeaver Moon (super moon): Peaks Nov. 24, at 9:53 a.m. ETCold Moon (super moon): Peaks Dec. 23, at 8:28 p.m. ET
